title.en: The Reprocessing System Ontology for a Circular Factory

description.en: Funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) - SFB 1574 - project ID 471687386.

comments.en:
Domain ontology of SFB 1574 subproject C02 (Reprocessing System). Formerly drafted under the namespace https://w3id.org/circularfactory/C02#. It extends the Circular Factory Core Ontology with the resources, processes, operations, process parameters, in-process observations, monitoring datasets and data-driven models of the semi-autonomous additive-subtractive reprocessing of unique metallic components (high-speed DED-LB/M combined with machining) in the InRePro cell.
Reuse strategy: Core, SOSA and PROV-O are imported. QUDT is referenced but not imported because of its size; load the QUDT schema and the quantity-kind and unit vocabularies into the triple store separately. Terms of the Perpetual Product Ontology are referenced but not imported, because version 0.0.1 re-declares Core properties with conflicting domains and ranges. The alignment to DOLCE+DnS Ultralite is provided in the separate module reprocessing-system-dul-alignment.ttl.
Extension point for causal knowledge (planned): process parameter settings (sosa:Actuation) and observations of deposit characteristics (sosa:Observation) are first-class individuals, so causal relations between them can be added later without changing existing terms.

editorialNote.value: OPEN ISSUE OI-3 (Core consistency): in Core 0.9.0, cfc:Component is unsatisfiable because cfc:hasOrigin has the two domains cfc:Assembly and cfc:Component, which are disjoint. This ontology follows the intended semantics (rps:ReprocessedComponent is a subclass of cfc:Component) and does not work around it. The modelling requirements of the Core are owned by A01; the correction is pending there.

OPEN ISSUE OI-2 (uncertainty representation): the representation of measurement and prediction uncertainty (qudt:standardUncertainty, rps:hasCoverageFactor, rps:hasConfidenceLevel, rps:hasLowerPredictionBound, rps:hasUpperPredictionBound, rps:hasUncertaintyEvaluationMethod, rps:UncertaintyEvaluationMethod) is accepted by INF for now but must be aligned with the uncertainty models of subprojects B03 and A03.

OPEN ISSUE OI-1 (sensor and measurement classes): rps:Sensor and rps:Measurement are defined locally as specialisations of sosa:Sensor and sosa:Result, as recommended by INF, because it is not yet decided whether every CRC subproject needs cfc:Sensor and cfc:Measurement in the Core. If such classes are added to the Core, rps:Sensor and rps:Measurement are to be aligned to them or deprecated.

OPEN ISSUE OI-5 (further domain ontologies): an alignment to Onto3D was requested but not yet carried out because the intended ontology and namespace could not be identified unambiguously. QUDT is referenced but not imported because of its size.

OPEN ISSUE OI-4 (Perpetual Product Ontology): version 0.0.1 is referenced but not imported, because it re-declares Core properties with domains and ranges that conflict with Core 0.9.0 (e.g. cfc:hasFinalWorkpiece). To be imported once the two ontologies are harmonised.

publisher.value: Collaborative Research Centre SFB 1574 Circular Factory for the Perpetual Product, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT)

title.value: The Reprocessing System Ontology for a Circular Factory

comment.en: The quality state of a workpiece after deposition, evaluated at a given time and supported by observations of deposit characteristics.
A time-resolved log of emission spectra recorded by an optical emission spectrometer.
An image sequence recorded by a high-speed camera.
A coaxial powder nozzle of a high-speed DED machine. Its abrasive wear changes the powder caustic and is assessed by powder caustic analysis before deposition.

definition.value: Person agents are people.

comment.en: The capability of the specialized machine cell to perform machining only, without additive build-up.

definition.value: An actuatable quality (property, characteristic) of a FeatureOfInterest.

example.value: A window actuator acts by changing the state between a frame and a window. The ability of the window to be opened and closed is its ActuatableProperty.

comment.en: An actuatable quality (property, characteristic) of a FeatureOfInterest.
The liquid metal region of the interaction zone during deposition, observed by pyrometry, high-speed imaging and emission spectroscopy.

High-speed directed energy deposition with laser beam and metal powder (HS DED-LB/M, EHLA), in which the powder focus lies above the melt pool so that the powder is largely molten before it reaches the substrate.
The second Fourier order of the powder caustic cross-section, used as an indicator of the condition of the powder nozzle.
The smallest diameter of the powder stream along its axis.
The axial distance of the powder stream waist from the nozzle tip.
An observable property of the powder stream that indicates the condition of the powder nozzle, e.g. caustic waist diameter or caustic ovality.

definition.value: A bundle is a named set of provenance descriptions, and is itself an Entity, so allowing provenance of provenance to be expressed.

comment.en: Note that there are kinds of bundles (e.g. handwritten letters, audio recordings, etc.) that are not expressed in PROV-O, but can be still be described by PROV-O.
A controllable property of a manufacturing process that is set by the machine control.
A physical measurement system of the reprocessing cell that observes the process, the powder stream or the workpiece. Portable systems may be moved between manufacturing resources.
The thickness of material removed in one machining pass.
The speed of the cutting edge relative to the workpiece.
The feed velocity of the tool relative to the workpiece.
The rotational frequency of the machine spindle.
A process parameter of milling or turning, e.g. cutting speed or depth of cut.

definition.value: An Actuation carries out an (Actuation) Procedure to change the state of the world using an Actuator.

example.value: The activity of automatically closing a window if the temperature in a room drops below 20 degree Celsius. The activity is the Actuation and the device that closes the window is the Actuator. The Procedure is the rule, plan, or specification that defines the conditions that triggers the Actuation, here a drop in temperature.

comment.en: An Actuation carries out an (Actuation) Procedure to change the state of the world using an Actuator.
The capability of a mill-turn machining centre to remove material by milling and turning.
The capability of a high-speed DED machine to deposit material by HS DED-LB/M.

definition.value: Communication is the exchange of an entity by two activities, one activity using the entity generated by the other.

comment.en: An instance of prov:Communication provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasInformedBy relation from an informed prov:Activity to the prov:Activity that informed it. For example, :you_jumping_off_bridge prov:wasInformedBy :everyone_else_jumping_off_bridge; prov:qualifiedCommunication [ a prov:Communication; prov:activity :everyone_else_jumping_off_bridge; :foo :bar ].

A production process that restores a damaged component by removing the damaged volume, rebuilding it by high-speed DED-LB/M and finish machining the functional surfaces. One component enters and one component leaves the process.

An operation dispatched by production control to the specialized machine cell to reprocess one component. Its IRI serves as correlation key between production control and subproject C02; it is decomposed into process runs.
A production process that removes material from a component by milling or turning.
A layer of material deposited onto a workpiece during one additive deposition run. Characteristics such as layer height or relative density are observed on it.

definition.value: An organization is a social or legal institution such as a company, society, etc.

comment.en: The time delay between a laser power step and the resulting emission response of the interaction zone.
The amplitude of the structure-borne sound signal of the acoustic emission system.
The temperature of the interaction zone as measured by two-colour pyrometry.
The width of the melt pool as derived from high-speed imaging.
An observable property of the running process itself, e.g. melt pool temperature, spectral lag or acoustic emission amplitude.

definition.value: An activity is something that occurs over a period of time and acts upon or with entities; it may include consuming, processing, transforming, modifying, relocating, using, or generating entities.

comment.en: A supporting process that characterises the powder caustic before deposition in order to assess the condition of the powder nozzle.
A stack of powder stream cross-section images recorded by a powder caustic analysis system.

definition.value: An entity is a physical, digital, conceptual, or other kind of thing with some fixed aspects; entities may be real or imaginary.
An act of Sampling carries out a sampling Procedure to create or transform one or more samples.

example.value: Establishing a station for environmental monitoring.
Taking a diamond-drill core from a rock outcrop.
Drawing blood from a patient.
Crushing a rock sample in a ball mill.
Digging a pit through a soil sequence.
Registering an image of the landscape.
Dividing a field site into quadrants.
Sieving a powder to separate the subset finer than 100-mesh.
Selecting a subset of a population.
Drilling an observation well.
Splitting a piece of drill-core to create two new samples.

comment.en: An act of Sampling carries out a sampling Procedure to create or transform one or more samples.

definition.value: Influence is the capacity of an entity, activity, or agent to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of another by means of usage, start, end, generation, invalidation, communication, derivation, attribution, association, or delegation.

comment.en: An instance of prov:Influence provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasInfluencedBy relation from some influenced Activity, Entity, or Agent to the influencing Activity, Entity, or Agent. For example, :stomach_ache prov:wasInfluencedBy :spoon; prov:qualifiedInfluence [ a prov:Influence; prov:entity :spoon; :foo :bar ] . Because prov:Influence is a broad relation, the more specific relations (Communication, Delegation, End, etc.) should be used when applicable.

definition.value: The Result of an Observation, Actuation, or act of Sampling. To store an observation's simple result value one can use the hasSimpleResult property.

example.value: The value 20 as the height of a certain tree together with the unit, e.g., Meter.

comment.en: The Result of an Observation, Actuation, or act of Sampling. To store an observation's simple result value one can use the hasSimpleResult property.
A documented signal or image processing procedure that derives a characteristic value from raw sensor data, e.g. the evaluation of the second Fourier order of the caustic cross-section.
The powder-gas jet leaving the powder nozzle, whose caustic (waist diameter, focus position, cross-section shape) is observed by powder caustic analysis.

editorialNote.value: OPEN ISSUE OI-3: unsatisfiable under Core 0.9.0 because cfc:Component is unsatisfiable there; correction pending in the Core.

comment.en: A component that is or was subject to a reprocessing operation. The component identity is managed by production control; this class adds the C02 view on it.
An executed, indivisible step of a reprocessing operation on one resource of the cell, for example one deposition run, one machining run or one monitoring run.

definition.value: Invalidation is the start of the destruction, cessation, or expiry of an existing entity by an activity. The entity is no longer available for use (or further invalidation) after invalidation. Any generation or usage of an entity precedes its invalidation.

comment.en: An instance of prov:Invalidation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasInvalidatedBy relation from an invalidated prov:Entity to the prov:Activity that invalidated it. For example, :uncracked_egg prov:wasInvalidatedBy :baking; prov:qualifiedInvalidation [ a prov:Invalidation; prov:activity :baking; :foo :bar ].

definition.value: A quotation is the repeat of (some or all of) an entity, such as text or image, by someone who may or may not be its original author. Quotation is a particular case of derivation.

comment.en: An instance of prov:Quotation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasQuotedFrom relation from some taken prov:Entity from an earlier, larger prov:Entity. For example, :here_is_looking_at_you_kid prov:wasQuotedFrom :casablanca_script; prov:qualifiedQuotation [ a prov:Quotation; prov:entity :casablanca_script; :foo :bar ].
A series of distance measurements recorded by an optical coherence tomography system.

definition.value:
A primary source for a topic refers to something produced by some agent with direct experience and knowledge about the topic, at the time of the topic's study, without benefit from hindsight.

Because of the directness of primary sources, they 'speak for themselves' in ways that cannot be captured through the filter of secondary sources. As such, it is important for secondary sources to reference those primary sources from which they were derived, so that their reliability can be investigated.

A primary source relation is a particular case of derivation of secondary materials from their primary sources. It is recognized that the determination of primary sources can be up to interpretation, and should be done according to conventions accepted within the application's domain.

comment.en: An instance of prov:PrimarySource provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:hadPrimarySource relation from some secondary prov:Entity to an earlier, primary prov:Entity. For example, :blog prov:hadPrimarySource :newsArticle; prov:qualifiedPrimarySource [ a prov:PrimarySource; prov:entity :newsArticle; :foo :bar ] .

definition.value: A revision is a derivation for which the resulting entity is a revised version of some original. The implication here is that the resulting entity contains substantial content from the original. Revision is a particular case of derivation.

comment.en: An instance of prov:Revision provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasRevisionOf relation from some newer prov:Entity to an earlier prov:Entity. For example, :draft_2 prov:wasRevisionOf :draft_1; prov:qualifiedRevision [ a prov:Revision; prov:entity :draft_1; :foo :bar ].
A laser triangulation sensor that captures the surface profile of deposited tracks and layers.

definition.value: A role is the function of an entity or agent with respect to an activity, in the context of a usage, generation, invalidation, association, start, and end.

comment.en: An inline interferometric distance measurement system (e.g. Precitec IDM1550) used for in-process measurement of layer height in high-speed DED-LB/M.
Machining that removes the damaged or affected volume of a component before additive build-up, based on inspection information on damage location and type.

definition.value: End is when an activity is deemed to have been ended by an entity, known as trigger. The activity no longer exists after its end. Any usage, generation, or invalidation involving an activity precedes the activity's end. An end may refer to a trigger entity that terminated the activity, or to an activity, known as ender that generated the trigger.

comment.en: An instance of prov:End provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasEndedBy relation from some ended prov:Activity to an prov:Entity that ended it. For example, :ball_game prov:wasEndedBy :buzzer; prov:qualifiedEnd [ a prov:End; prov:entity :buzzer; :foo :bar; prov:atTime '2012-03-09T08:05:08-05:00'^^xsd:dateTime ].

definition.value: A device that is used by, or implements, a Sampling Procedure to create or transform one or more samples.

example.value: A ball mill, diamond drill, hammer, hypodermic syringe and needle, image Sensor or a soil auger can all act as sampling devices (i.e., be Samplers). However, sometimes the distinction between the Sampler and the Sensor is not evident, as they are packaged as a unit. A Sampler need not be a physical device.

comment.en: A device that is used by, or implements, a Sampling Procedure to create or transform one or more samples.
A set of surface profiles recorded by a laser line scanner.
A supporting process in which one or more measurement systems observe a deposition or machining process without changing the workpiece.

The setting of one process parameter to a nominal value by a manufacturing resource during a process run. The nominal value is given as qudt:QuantityValue via sosa:hasResult. Settings are individuals so that they can later serve as causes in causal relations.
A light-section system (e.g. ponticon PowderSpy) that images cross-sections of the powder stream to characterise the powder caustic and the nozzle condition.
A batch of metal powder used as filler material in high-speed DED-LB/M, characterised among others by its particle size distribution.
A data-driven process model based on partial least squares (PLS) regression.
A machine for high-speed directed energy deposition with laser beam and metal powder (HS DED-LB/M, EHLA), e.g. the 5-axis pE3D system of ponticon GmbH in the InRePro cell.
The part of the manufacturing history of a component that documents the reprocessing operations it has undergone in the specialized machine cell.
A coaxial ratio pyrometer measuring the temperature of the interaction zone largely independently of emissivity.

definition.value: The PROV data model is implicitly based on a notion of instantaneous events (or just events), that mark transitions in the world. Events include generation, usage, or invalidation of entities, as well as starting or ending of activities. This notion of event is not first-class in the data model, but it is useful for explaining its other concepts and its semantics.

comment.en: An instantaneous event, or event for short, happens in the world and marks a change in the world, in its activities and in its entities. The term 'event' is commonly used in process algebra with a similar meaning. Events represent communications or interactions; they are assumed to be atomic and instantaneous.

editorsDefinition.value: ActivitiyInfluence is the capacity of an activity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of another by means of generation, invalidation, communication, or other.

comment.en: It is not recommended that the type ActivityInfluence be asserted without also asserting one of its more specific subclasses.
An observation made by a physical measurement system of the reprocessing cell. The result is given as qudt:QuantityValue, optionally with its measurement uncertainty.

definition.value: Act of carrying out an (Observation) Procedure to estimate or calculate a value of a property of a FeatureOfInterest. Links to a Sensor to describe what made the Observation and how; links to an ObservableProperty to describe what the result is an estimate of, and to a FeatureOfInterest to detail what that property was associated with.

example.value: The activity of estimating the intensity of an Earthquake using the Mercalli intensity scale is an Observation as is measuring the moment magnitude, i.e., the energy released by said earthquake.

comment.en: Act of carrying out an (Observation) Procedure to estimate or calculate a value of a property of a FeatureOfInterest. Links to a Sensor to describe what made the Observation and how; links to an ObservableProperty to describe what the result is an estimate of, and to a FeatureOfInterest to detail what that property was associated with.

The InRePro reprocessing cell of subproject C02 as the single externally addressed resource of the circular factory. It receives reprocessing operations from production control and decides internally on the sequence of process runs and the measurement systems involved. Replaces the middleware term 'SpecializedMachines' (singular noun required by the SFB modeling convention).
The particle diameter below which 90 % of the powder volume lies.
The particle diameter below which 10 % of the powder volume lies.
The median particle diameter of the powder volume distribution.
An observable property of the metal powder feedstock, e.g. a characteristic value of the particle size distribution.
The nominal output power of the processing laser.
The mass of powder fed through the nozzle per unit time.
The relative speed between deposition head and substrate surface; in high-speed DED-LB/M typically tens of metres per minute.
The volume flow rate of the inert gas shielding the interaction zone.
The lateral distance between the centre lines of adjacent deposition tracks.
The volume flow rate of the gas transporting the powder to the nozzle.
The distance between nozzle tip and substrate surface.
The diameter of the laser beam on the substrate surface.
A process parameter of high-speed DED-LB/M, e.g. laser power, processing speed or powder mass flow rate.
A spectrometer for synchronised multispectral emission analysis of the interaction zone, used among others to determine the spectral lag.
A machine tool for milling and turning used for damage removal before and finish machining after deposition, e.g. the 5-axis DMU 60 eVo of DMG MORI in the InRePro cell.

definition.value: An empty collection is a collection without members.
An agent is something that bears some form of responsibility for an activity taking place, for the existence of an entity, or for another agent's activity.

comment.en: A statistical or machine-learning model that predicts deposit characteristics from process parameters and process monitoring features. Modelled as a virtual sensor in the sense of SOSA.

definition.value: A location can be an identifiable geographic place (ISO 19112), but it can also be a non-geographic place such as a directory, row, or column. As such, there are numerous ways in which location can be expressed, such as by a coordinate, address, landmark, and so forth.
A derivation is a transformation of an entity into another, an update of an entity resulting in a new one, or the construction of a new entity based on a pre-existing entity.

comment.en: An instance of prov:Derivation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasDerivedFrom relation from some derived prov:Entity to another prov:Entity from which it was derived. For example, :chewed_bubble_gum prov:wasDerivedFrom :unwrapped_bubble_gum; prov:qualifiedDerivation [ a prov:Derivation; prov:entity :unwrapped_bubble_gum; :foo :bar ].
A process run in which material is deposited by high-speed DED-LB/M.

definition.value: Start is when an activity is deemed to have been started by an entity, known as trigger. The activity did not exist before its start. Any usage, generation, or invalidation involving an activity follows the activity's start. A start may refer to a trigger entity that set off the activity, or to an activity, known as starter, that generated the trigger.

comment.en: An instance of prov:Start provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasStartedBy relation from some started prov:Activity to an prov:Entity that started it. For example, :foot_race prov:wasStartedBy :bang; prov:qualifiedStart [ a prov:Start; prov:entity :bang; :foo :bar; prov:atTime '2012-03-09T08:05:08-05:00'^^xsd:dateTime ] .
The capability of a measurement system to observe a deposition or machining process.
A process run in which a measurement system records data during or before a deposition or machining run.

definition.value: Device, agent (including humans), or software (simulation) involved in, or implementing, a Procedure. Sensors respond to a stimulus, e.g., a change in the environment, or input data composed from the results of prior Observations, and generate a Result. Sensors can be hosted by Platforms.

example.value: Accelerometers, gyroscopes, barometers, magnetometers, and so forth are Sensors that are typically mounted on a modern smart phone (which acts as Platform). Other examples of sensors include the human eyes.

comment.en: Device, agent (including humans), or software (simulation) involved in, or implementing, a Procedure. Sensors respond to a stimulus, e.g., a change in the environment, or input data composed from the results of prior Observations, and generate a Result. Sensors can be hosted by Platforms.

editorialNote.value: OPEN ISSUE OI-2: to be aligned with the uncertainty models of B03 and A03.

comment.en: Uncertainty of a model-based prediction estimated from the cross-validated prediction error of the data-driven process model.
Uncertainty evaluated by means other than statistical analysis of observations, e.g. from manufacturer specifications or calibration certificates (JCGM 100:2008).
Uncertainty evaluated by statistical analysis of a series of observations (JCGM 100:2008).
The method by which the uncertainty stated for a quantity value was obtained.

definition.value:
Attribution is the ascribing of an entity to an agent.

When an entity e is attributed to agent ag, entity e was generated by some unspecified activity that in turn was associated to agent ag. Thus, this relation is useful when the activity is not known, or irrelevant.

comment.en: An instance of prov:Attribution provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasAttributedTo relation from an prov:Entity to some prov:Agent that had some responsible for it. For example, :cake prov:wasAttributedTo :baker; prov:qualifiedAttribution [ a prov:Attribution; prov:entity :baker; :foo :bar ].

definition.value: A plan is an entity that represents a set of actions or steps intended by one or more agents to achieve some goals.

comment.en: There exist no prescriptive requirement on the nature of plans, their representation, the actions or steps they consist of, or their intended goals. Since plans may evolve over time, it may become necessary to track their provenance, so plans themselves are entities. Representing the plan explicitly in the provenance can be useful for various tasks: for example, to validate the execution as represented in the provenance record, to manage expectation failures, or to provide explanations.

definition.value: A device that is used by, or implements, an (Actuation) Procedure that changes the state of the world.

example.value: A window actuator for automatic window control, i.e., opening or closing the window.

comment.en: A device that is used by, or implements, an (Actuation) Procedure that changes the state of the world.
A process run in which material is removed by milling or turning.

definition.value: An activity association is an assignment of responsibility to an agent for an activity, indicating that the agent had a role in the activity. It further allows for a plan to be specified, which is the plan intended by the agent to achieve some goals in the context of this activity.

comment.en: An instance of prov:Association provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasAssociatedWith relation from an prov:Activity to some prov:Agent that had some responsiblity for it. For example, :baking prov:wasAssociatedWith :baker; prov:qualifiedAssociation [ a prov:Association; prov:agent :baker; :foo :bar ].

definition.value: Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation.

comment.en: An instance of prov:Generation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasGeneratedBy relation from a generated prov:Entity to the prov:Activity that generated it. For example, :cake prov:wasGeneratedBy :baking; prov:qualifiedGeneration [ a prov:Generation; prov:activity :baking; :foo :bar ].
A structure-borne sound sensor system (e.g. QASS). It is the only measurement system used in both deposition and machining and is remounted between the two machines.

editorsDefinition.value: AgentInfluence is the capacity of an agent to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of another by means of attribution, association, delegation, or other.

comment.en: It is not recommended that the type AgentInfluence be asserted without also asserting one of its more specific subclasses.

editorsDefinition.value: EntityInfluence is the capacity of an entity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of another by means of usage, start, end, derivation, or other.

comment.en: It is not recommended that the type EntityInfluence be asserted without also asserting one of its more specific subclasses.

definition.value: A software agent is running software.

note.value: Many observations may be created via the same Procedure, the same way as many tables are assembled using the same instructions (as information objects, not their concrete realization).

definition.value: A workflow, protocol, plan, algorithm, or computational method specifying how to make an Observation, create a Sample, or make a change to the state of the world (via an Actuator). A Procedure is re-usable, and might be involved in many Observations, Samplings, or Actuations. It explains the steps to be carried out to arrive at reproducible results.

example.value: The measured wind speed differs depending on the height of the sensor above the surface, e.g., due to friction. Consequently, procedures for measuring wind speed define a standard height for anemometers above ground, typically 10m for meteorological measures and 2m in Agrometeorology. This definition of height, sensor placement, and so forth are defined by the Procedure.

comment.en: A workflow, protocol, plan, algorithm, or computational method specifying how to make an Observation, create a Sample, or make a change to the state of the world (via an Actuator). A Procedure is re-usable, and might be involved in many Observations, Samplings, or Actuations. It explains the steps to be carried out to arrive at reproducible results.

definition.value: A collection is an entity that provides a structure to some constituents, which are themselves entities. These constituents are said to be member of the collections.

note.value: A transient sample, such as a ships-track or flight-line, might be identified and described, but is unlikely to be revisited exactly.

definition.value: Feature which is intended to be representative of a FeatureOfInterest on which Observations may be made.

example.value: A statistical sample is often designed to be characteristic of an entire population, so that observations can be made regarding the sample that provide a good estimate of the properties of the population.

A 'station' is essentially an identifiable locality where a sensor system or Procedure may be deployed and an observation made. In the context of the observation model, it connotes the 'world in the vicinity of the station', so the observed properties relate to the physical medium at the station, and not to any physical artifact such as a mooring, buoy, benchmark, monument, well, etc.

comment.en:
Samples are artifacts of an observational strategy, and have no significant function outside of their role in the observation process. The characteristics of the samples themselves are of little interest, except perhaps to the manager of a sampling campaign.

A Sample is intended to sample some FatureOfInterest, so there is an expectation of at least one isSampleOf property. However, in some cases the identity, and even the exact type, of the sampled feature may not be known when observations are made using the sampling features.
The capability of the specialized machine cell to reprocess a damaged component by damage removal, high-speed DED-LB/M build-up and finish machining.
Machining after additive build-up that restores the geometry and surface of the functional surfaces.
A camera for high-speed imaging of the melt pool and the powder-laser interaction.
The cumulative height of the deposited material above the substrate.
The height increment of one deposited layer, measured in-process by OCT or after deposition by laser line scanning.

The ratio of the density of the deposited material to the density of the fully dense material. Reference measurements are provided by material characterisation (subproject B02); C02 provides model-based predictions.

The Vickers hardness of the deposited material. Reference measurements are provided by material characterisation (subproject B02); C02 provides model-based predictions. No QUDT quantity kind is assigned because hardness scales are not physical quantities in the sense of the SI.
The width of a single deposited track.
An observable property of deposited material, e.g. layer height, track width or relative density.

definition.value:
Delegation is the assignment of authority and responsibility to an agent (by itself or by another agent) to carry out a specific activity as a delegate or representative, while the agent it acts on behalf of retains some responsibility for the outcome of the delegated work.

For example, a student acted on behalf of his supervisor, who acted on behalf of the department chair, who acted on behalf of the university; all those agents are responsible in some way for the activity that took place but we do not say explicitly who bears responsibility and to what degree.

comment.en: An instance of prov:Delegation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:actedOnBehalfOf relation from a performing prov:Agent to some prov:Agent for whom it was performed. For example, :mixing prov:wasAssociatedWith :toddler . :toddler prov:actedOnBehalfOf :mother; prov:qualifiedDelegation [ a prov:Delegation; prov:entity :mother; :foo :bar ].
A machine of the reprocessing cell that changes the geometry or material state of a workpiece and hosts measurement systems.
A temperature time series recorded by a two-colour pyrometer.

An estimate of an observable property made by a data-driven process model (virtual sensor) from process parameter settings and process monitoring observations. The result carries the prediction uncertainty.

editorialNote.value: OPEN ISSUE OI-1: local class recommended by INF while it is open whether a measurement class is added to the Core. OPEN ISSUE OI-2: whether quantity-value results of observations shall additionally be typed as rps:Measurement is to be decided together with the uncertainty alignment with B03 and A03.

comment.en: Data produced by a measurement observation.
An empirical regression model derived from a design of experiments, e.g. a central composite design.

definition.value: An observable quality (property, characteristic) of a FeatureOfInterest.

example.value: The height of a tree, the depth of a water body, or the temperature of a surface are examples of observable properties, while the value of a classic car is not (directly) observable but asserted.

comment.en: An observable quality (property, characteristic) of a FeatureOfInterest.
A structure-borne sound recording of an acoustic emission system.

definition.value: A Platform is an entity that hosts other entities, particularly Sensors, Actuators, Samplers, and other Platforms.

example.value: A post, buoy, vehicle, ship, aircraft, satellite, cell-phone, human or animal may act as platforms for (technical or biological) sensors or actuators.

comment.en: A Platform is an entity that hosts other entities, particularly Sensors, Actuators, Samplers, and other Platforms.
A raw data artifact recorded by a measurement system during a process run. Only the storage location of the raw data is kept in the knowledge graph. Replaces the middleware term 'Dataset'.

definition.value: The thing whose property is being estimated or calculated in the course of an Observation to arrive at a Result or whose property is being manipulated by an Actuator, or which is being sampled or transformed in an act of Sampling.

example.value: When measuring the height of a tree, the height is the observed ObservableProperty, 20m may be the Result of the Observation, and the tree is the FeatureOfInterest. A window is a FeatureOfInterest for an automatic window control Actuator.

comment.en: The thing whose property is being estimated or calculated in the course of an Observation to arrive at a Result or whose property is being manipulated by an Actuator, or which is being sampled or transformed in an act of Sampling.

editorialNote.value: OPEN ISSUE OI-1: local class recommended by INF while it is open whether a sensor class is added to the Core.

comment.en: Any physical or virtual device, agent or software that observes a property in the C02 reprocessing context.

definition.value: Usage is the beginning of utilizing an entity by an activity. Before usage, the activity had not begun to utilize this entity and could not have been affected by the entity.

comment.en: An instance of prov:Usage provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:used relation from some prov:Activity to an prov:Entity that it used. For example, :keynote prov:used :podium; prov:qualifiedUsage [ a prov:Usage; prov:entity :podium; :foo :bar ].

definition.value: An entity that is a specialization of another shares all aspects of the latter, and additionally presents more specific aspects of the same thing as the latter. In particular, the lifetime of the entity being specialized contains that of any specialization. Examples of aspects include a time period, an abstraction, and a context associated with the entity.

editorialNote.value: The naming of prov:atLocation parallels prov:atTime, and is not named prov:hadLocation to avoid conflicting with the convention that prov:had* properties are used on prov:Influence classes.
This property is not functional because the many values could be at a variety of granularies (In this building, in this room, in that chair).

comment.en: The Location of any resource.
comment.undefined: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

editorialNote.value: It is the intent that the property chain holds: (prov:qualifiedEnd o prov:atTime) rdfs:subPropertyOf prov:endedAtTime.

comment.en: The time at which an activity ended. See also prov:startedAtTime.
If this Activity prov:wasInformedBy Activity :a, then it can qualify how it was influenced using prov:qualifiedCommunication [ a prov:Communication;  prov:activity :a; :foo :bar ].

definition.value: Relation between a Sensor, Actuator, Sampler, or Platform, and the Platform that it is mounted on or hosted by.

comment.en: Relation between a Sensor, Actuator, Sampler, or Platform, and the Platform that it is mounted on or hosted by.

Relates a measurement system to the manufacturing resource on which it is currently mounted. Relevant for portable systems such as the acoustic emission system. Replaces the middleware term 'currentlyMountedOn'.
If this Agent prov:actedOnBehalfOf Agent :ag, then it can qualify how with prov:qualifiedResponsibility [ a prov:Responsibility;  prov:agent :ag; :foo :bar ].
The time at which an InstantaneousEvent occurred, in the form of xsd:dateTime.

definition.value: A relation between an Observation and the entity whose quality was observed, or between an Actuation and the entity whose property was modified, or between an act of Sampling and the entity that was sampled.

example.value: For example, in an Observation of the weight of a person, the FeatureOfInterest is the person and the property is its weight.

comment.en: A relation between an Observation and the entity whose quality was observed, or between an Actuation and the entity whose property was modified, or between an act of Sampling and the entity that was sampled.
Relates a process run to the reprocessing operation it belongs to. Replaces the middleware term 'partOfReprocessingOperation'.
Relates a component to its reprocessing history.
If this Entity prov:wasRevisionOf Entity :e, then it can qualify how it was revised using prov:qualifiedRevision [ a prov:Revision;  prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].
If this Entity prov:wasInvalidatedBy Activity :a, then it can qualify how it was invalidated using prov:qualifiedInvalidation [ a prov:Invalidation;  prov:activity :a; :foo :bar ].

definition.value: A relation to link to a re-usable Procedure used in making an Observation, an Actuation, or a Sample, typically through a Sensor, Actuator or Sampler.

comment.en: A relation to link to a re-usable Procedure used in making an Observation, an Actuation, or a Sample, typically through a Sensor, Actuator or Sampler.
Relates a high-speed DED machine to the powder nozzle currently installed on it.
The position of a process run within its reprocessing operation. Replaces the middleware term 'stepOrder'.
If this Entity prov:wasDerivedFrom Entity :e, then it can qualify how it was derived using prov:qualifiedDerivation [ a prov:Derivation;  prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].
Start is when an activity is deemed to have started. A start may refer to an entity, known as trigger, that initiated the activity.

Shortcut for the mean layer height in micrometres derived from an OCT measurement series. Kept for compatibility with the C02 middleware ('layerHeight'); the canonical representation is a process monitoring observation of rps:LayerHeight with a qudt:QuantityValue result.
If this Activity prov:wasEndedBy Entity :e1, then it can qualify how it was ended using prov:qualifiedEnd [ a prov:End;  prov:entity :e1; :foo :bar ].
An prov:Agent that had some (unspecified) responsibility for the occurrence of this prov:Activity.

definition.value: Relation linking an act of Sampling to the Sampler (sampling device or entity) that made it.

comment.en: Relation linking an act of Sampling to the Sampler (sampling device or entity) that made it.
A revision is a derivation that revises an entity into a revised version.

comment.en: The upper bound of the prediction interval of a model-based prediction, in the unit of the quantity value.

editorialNote.value: OPEN ISSUE OI-2: to be aligned with the uncertainty models of B03 and A03.

comment.en: The coverage factor k used to obtain an expanded uncertainty from the standard uncertainty (qudt:standardUncertainty) according to the GUM.
If this Entity prov:wasAttributedTo Agent :ag, then it can qualify how it was influenced using prov:qualifiedAttribution [ a prov:Attribution;  prov:agent :ag; :foo :bar ].
The coefficient of determination R² of a data-driven process model on its training data.

definition.value: Relation linking an Actuation to the Actuator that made that Actuation.

definition.value: Relation between an Observation and the Sensor which made the Observation.

comment.en: Relation between an Observation and the Sensor which made the Observation.

definition.value: Relation between an Actuation and the property of a FeatureOfInterest it is acting upon.

example.value: In the activity (Actuation) of automatically closing a window if the temperature in a room drops below 20 degrees Celsius, the property on which the Actuator acts upon is the state of the window as it changes from being open to being closed.

comment.en: Relation between an Actuation and the property of a FeatureOfInterest it is acting upon.
The batch or lot number of a powder feedstock.

definition.value: Relation from a Sample to the FeatureOfInterest that it is intended to be representative of.

Relates a process monitoring dataset to the measurement system that recorded it.

definition.value: Relation between an Observation and the Sensor which made the Observation.

The _optional_ Generation involved in an Entity's Derivation.

comment.en: The time at which an activity started. See also prov:endedAtTime.
An entity is derived from an original entity by copying, or 'quoting', some or all of it.
A prov:Entity that was used by this prov:Activity. For example, :baking prov:used :spoon, :egg, :oven .
The _optional_ Usage involved in an Entity's Derivation.

editorialNote.value: This property behaves in spirit like rdf:object; it references the object of a prov:wasInfluencedBy triple.

editorsDefinition.value: The prov:agent property references an prov:Agent which influenced a resource. This property applies to an prov:AgentInfluence, which is given by a subproperty of prov:qualifiedInfluence from the influenced prov:Entity, prov:Activity or prov:Agent.

definition.value: Relation between an Actuator and the Actuation it has made.

definition.value: Two alternate entities present aspects of the same thing. These aspects may be the same or different, and the alternate entities may or may not overlap in time.

comment.en: Relates a data-driven process model to a dataset used for its training.

Relates an observation whose result was derived by feature extraction to the raw dataset it was computed from.
Relates a model-based prediction to an observation used as model input.

definition.value: The result time is the instant of time when the Observation, Actuation or Sampling activity was completed.

comment.en: The result time is the instant of time when the Observation, Actuation or Sampling activity was completed.
The position of a deposited layer in the build-up sequence, starting with 1.

comment.en: Relation between a Sensor and an Observation made by the Sensor.
Because prov:qualifiedInfluence is a broad relation, the more specific relations (qualifiedCommunication, qualifiedDelegation, qualifiedEnd, etc.) should be used when applicable.

definition.value: Relation linking an Observation to the property that was observed. The ObservableProperty should be a property of the FeatureOfInterest (linked by hasFeatureOfInterest) of this Observation.

comment.en: Relation linking an Observation to the property that was observed. The ObservableProperty should be a property of the FeatureOfInterest (linked by hasFeatureOfInterest) of this Observation.

Relates a model-based prediction to a process parameter setting used as model input.

comment.en: A relation between a FeatureOfInterest and an Observation about it, an Actuation acting on it, or an act of Sampling that sampled it.
Relates a process run to a nominal process parameter setting applied in it.

editorialNote.value: It is the intent that the property chain holds: (prov:qualifiedGeneration o prov:atTime) rdfs:subPropertyOf prov:generatedAtTime.

comment.en: The time at which an entity was completely created and is available for use.

editorialNote.value: This property serves the same purpose as rdf:value, but has been reintroduced to avoid some of the definitional ambiguity in the RDF specification (specifically, 'may be used in describing structured values').
The editor's definition comes from http://www.w3.org/TR/rdf-primer/#rdfvalue

definition.value: Provides a value that is a direct representation of an entity.

editorialNote.value: prov:invalidated is one of few inverse property defined, to allow Activity-oriented assertions in addition to Entity-oriented assertions.

comment.en: Relates an additive deposition run to the powder batch it consumed.

definition.value: Relation between a Sampler (sampling device or entity) and the Sampling act it performed.

definition.value: Relation linking a Result to the Observation or Actuation or act of Sampling that created or caused it.

The standardised designation of the powder alloy, e.g. a material number.

editorialNote.value:
The sub-properties of prov:wasInfluencedBy can be elaborated in more detail using the Qualification Pattern. For example, the binary relation :baking prov:used :spoon can be qualified by asserting :baking prov:qualifiedUsage [ a prov:Usage; prov:entity :spoon; prov:atLocation :kitchen ] .

Subproperties of prov:wasInfluencedBy may also be asserted directly without being qualified.

prov:wasInfluencedBy should not be used without also using one of its subproperties.

comment.en: Because prov:wasInfluencedBy is a broad relation, its more specific subproperties (e.g. prov:wasInformedBy, prov:actedOnBehalfOf, prov:wasEndedBy, etc.) should be used when applicable.

comment.en: Subproperties of prov:influencer are used to cite the object of an unqualified PROV-O triple whose predicate is a subproperty of prov:wasInfluencedBy (e.g. prov:used, prov:wasGeneratedBy). prov:influencer is used much like rdf:object is used.
